The Linux kernel is the core of the Linux operating system:
it manages processes, memory and device drivers while user-space
programs talk to it through system calls.
The Linux kernel is a free and open-source, monolithic, modular, multitasking Unix-like
kernel that is deployed on a wide variety of systems.
Linux began in 1991 with Linus Torvalds' first kernel release for the Intel 386
